title: runner.yaml
description: The machine's runner file, under the user's configuration directory alone: what qory run does on this machine. egress is the run policy's egress section and server the server document, both in the runner contract's grammar, https://qory.dev/contracts/runner/v1/. wall is the container the runtime is started in, that contract's wall.

server.description: The server every run on this machine reports to, the runner contract's server.schema.json: the runner fetches its configuration, signed, posts the events where it says and takes its run configuration as the policy. Absent, the events go to files alone.

url.description: https, or http to this machine; a scheme and a host with nothing after.

access_key.description: The key the server issued this machine: ak_ and 16 characters of lower-case Crockford base32.

secret.description: At least 16 characters; may be left out when QORY_SERVER_SECRET is set in the environment. It signs every request and is never sent.

run.description: What holds for every run on this machine unless a flag of qory run says otherwise.

timeout.description: How long a runtime may run, as a duration: 5h30m. At the limit the runner stops it and dev.qory.run.exited says so. Default no limit. --timeout names another for one run.

stop_signal.description: The signal that asks a runtime to leave when the runner stops it, at the limit or on a signal to qory run. Runtimes differ in what a signal means, so the runtime's descriptor says which, and this key names another for every run on the machine. Default the descriptor's, and SIGTERM when it names none. --stop-signal names another for one run.

stop_grace.description: How long a runtime gets between the stop signal and SIGKILL when the runner stops it, at the limit or on a signal to qory run: the time a session needs to close what it has open. Default the runtime's descriptor's, and 10s when it names none. --stop-grace names another for one run.

wall.description: The wall every run on this machine starts the runtime behind: a container with no route out except to the runner's proxy. Absent, the runtime is a process of this machine.

image.description: The agent's image: the runtime and the project's toolchain. qory builds none. May be left out when --image names one.

command.description: The program the adapter runs, podman say. Default docker.

helper.description: The absolute path of a static Linux build of qory, mounted read-only into the container as the relay and the hook forwarder. Default this binary, which only a Linux machine can use.

env.description: Names of variables of qory run's environment that go into the container, the model credential say. Values are never written here. Nothing else of the environment goes in.

user.description: The uid:gid the container runs as. Default qory run's own, so the checkout's files keep their owner. Root is refused; a machine where qory runs as root names another.

mounts.description: What the container sees of this machine beside the checkout and the composed home, each at its own path: an absolute path, with :ro after it for one the container cannot change. --mount adds to them. A socket, or a directory holding a container runtime's, is refused.

cpus.description: How many processors' worth of time the container gets, a decimal number. Default the engine's.

memory.description: The most memory the container gets: a number of bytes with an optional unit of b, k, m or g. Default the engine's.

pids_limit.description: The most processes and threads in the container. Default the engine's.

shm_size.description: The size of /dev/shm in the container, written as memory is. A browser needs more than an engine's default.

ca_env.description: The variables that point a program in the container at the bundle of authorities it trusts, the image's own and the run's, when a run has an authority of its own. Default SSL_CERT_FILE, GIT_SSL_CAINFO, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE.

credentials.description: The credentials this machine has for its runs, by name. A run's policy selects among them and defines none. Behind a wall the runner keeps each outside the container and its proxy sets it on the requests to the hosts it is for, ending the container's TLS for those hosts alone. Exactly one of env, file and adapter says where the token comes from.

env.description: A variable of qory run's environment that holds the token.

file.description: The absolute path of a file that holds the token, read again whenever it is used.

adapter.description: A program of yours, by its absolute path, and its arguments: it knows one kind of host, a source code host say, runs outside the container, and prints one JSON document, the runner contract's credential.schema.json: the token, when it expires, and the hosts, the scheme and the paths it is for. ${argument} in an argument is replaced by the argument the run's policy gives. The runner asks again before the token expires and when a host refuses it.

argument.description: A regular expression the policy's argument must match whole, with an adapter. Absent, a policy passes none.

hosts.description: With env or file, the hosts the token is for. With an adapter, the most it may claim.

paths.description: With env or file, the paths of the hosts the run may ask for, a path matched whole or up to a final * as a prefix; absent is every path. With an adapter, the most it may claim.

auth.description: With env or file, how the token is set: bearer, basic with a username, or header with a header's name.

placeholders.description: Variables the container gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that does not start without one set; the proxy replaces what the program sends.

integrations.description: The integrations this machine declares, by key: programs that speak the integration contract, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/. qory runs <program> describe, checks the settings against the description, and expands each role it knows; the credential role defines the credential named by the key, unless credentials defines that name itself. An integration that plays no role qory knows is refused.

program.description: The program: an absolute path, or a name looked up on the PATH. Default qory-<key>. qory runs it from outside the checkout; it and every directory above it belong to root or the user running qory, and only root's, wheel, admin or the owner's own group may write them besides the owner.

settings.description: The settings document, which the description's settings schema checks; absent is {}. It goes on the command line of every role, so it holds no value of a writeOnly setting: a secret is given as the file that holds it, <name>_file.
